messages.subject: Mutliple Group Expected Score Graph
parts:
All,
I have a questions about graphing the expected total scores for DTF in the MIRT package. I have two groups, Student and Programmers, that have taken the same test. I tested for DTF and found that I had significant DTF. I also plotted the the test score functions, as seen in the code below. All of this went well. My question is whether it is possible to separate the test score functions with their associated errors into different graphs. The DTF(mod, draws = 300, plot='func') shows both lines and their associated error. I want each line and its associated error in a different graph for comparison purposes. I know there is the extract.group function, which I have used to plot  the test score functions separately, but when I try to add the CI it does not graph the CIs just the test score functions (see last chunk of code). Any help would be greatly appreciated. Thanks in advance for any help.
-Gene

diff.1 <- dataPTS1[1:400, c(5,6,8,9,10,11)]
dataPTS1$sample[dataPTS1$sample==1] <- "Student"
dataPTS1$sample[dataPTS1$sample==2] <- "Programmer"
group <- dataPTS1$sample
mod <- multipleGroup(diff.1, 1, group = group, SE=TRUE,
                     invariance = c(colnames(diff.1)[1:2], 'free_means', 'free_var'))
coef(mod, simplify=TRUE, IRTpars= TRUE )
DTF(mod, draws = 300, plot='func')

group.1<-extract.group(mod,1)
summary(group.1)
plot(group.1, CI=0.95)

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: Mutliple Group Expected Score Graph
parts:
Probably the easiest way to do this would be if it were supported internally. Extracting the functional confidence intervals is a little awkward and would require saving the lattice objects and extracting the associated data stored within them (it's possible, and there are examples of this on the forum....but it's certainly ad hoc). I can add a facet-like argument to these plot functions to do this automatically, and would be happy to add this to the TODO list if that's what you're really looking for. HTH.

Phil
